title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CARLA'S BOOK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Carla Benson, forty-one, a tow truck driver in Boise, Idaho.
On long nights waiting for calls, she decided to write a whole book.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE PAPERBACKS
segments.quote: If you find a book you really want to read but it hasn't been written yet, then you must write it.
segments.author: Toni Morrison
lines: Carla loved mystery novels.
But none of them had a hero like her. A tired woman with a tow hook and a thermos.
Then she saw words from the novelist Toni Morrison:
If you find a book you really want to read but it hasn't been written yet, then you must write it.
That night, she wrote page one on the back of a tow ticket.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: NO MAP
segments.quote: It's like driving a car at night. You never see further than your headlights, but you can make the whole trip that way.
segments.author: E. L. Doctorow
lines: Trouble was, she had no idea who the killer was.
Then she read what the writer E. L. Doctorow said about writing:
It's like driving a car at night. You never see further than your headlights, but you can make the whole trip that way.
Carla knew night driving. So she stopped planning, and wrote one scene between every call.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE LAUGH
segments.quote: Life is not easy for any of us. But what of that? We must have perseverance and above all confidence in ourselves.
segments.author: Marie Curie
lines: At the yard, her coworker Duane found the notebook and read it out loud. Everybody laughed.
Carla went home ready to throw it away.
Her mom had a magnet on the fridge with words from the scientist Marie Curie:
Life is not easy for any of us. But what of that? We must have perseverance and above all confidence in ourselves.
Carla picked up the pen. And she named the villain Duane.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BORING PART
segments.quote: I try to leave out the parts readers skip.
segments.author: Elmore Leonard
lines: A year later, she gave all four hundred pages to her neighbor, Mrs. Ortiz.
Mrs. Ortiz fell asleep in chapter nine. Twice.
So Carla read advice from crime writer Elmore Leonard:
I try to leave out the parts readers skip.
She cut one hundred pages. Mrs. Ortiz stayed up till two in the morning.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THIRTY NO'S
segments.quote: Let me tell you the secret that has led me to my goal. My strength lies solely in my tenacity.
segments.author: Louis Pasteur
lines: She sent it to book agents. Thirty said no.
Carla taped every letter inside her truck, like a scoreboard.
Next to them, she taped words from Louis Pasteur, the French scientist:
Let me tell you the secret that has led me to my goal. My strength lies solely in my tenacity.
Letter thirty-one said yes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE READING
segments.quote: As long as you live, keep learning how to live.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: At her first reading at the Boise library, an old mechanic named Walt raised his hand.
He was seventy-eight, and said it was too late to write his life story.
Carla smiled and gave him a line from Seneca, the Roman thinker:
As long as you live, keep learning how to live.
Then she handed him a blank tow ticket. Page one.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start it. Keep going. Trust yourself. Cut the dull parts. Never quit. Pass it on.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start the book. Go one mile at a time. Trust yourself. Cut the dull parts. Don't quit. Help the next person start.
Me? I've started three books. All three are just the word lasagna.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
